docs.title: 🌌 Multi-Language DSA Learning Vault & Master Roadmap
docs.text:
Welcome to the ultimate Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA) Learning Vault. This repository is a topic-driven curriculum designed to take you from core computational foundations to advanced query optimizations.

Every topic contains clean, well-documented implementations across four primary interview languages: Python, C++, Java, and JavaScript (Node.js). Each solution comes with a built-in test driver so it can be run out of the box immediately.

docs.title: 🗺️ Master Curriculum Roadmap
docs.text: Module Core Topics Covered Languages Available 00-Foundations-and-Complexity Big-O analysis, memory models, math basics, pattern printing. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 01-Arrays-and-Strings 1D/2D arrays, matrix operations, two-pointers, sliding window. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 02-Linked-Lists Singly, Doubly, and Circular Linked Lists. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 03-Stacks-and-Queues Stacks, Queues, Deques, Balanced parentheses. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 04-Trees-and-BST Tree traversals (In/Pre/Post), Binary Search Trees. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 05-Heaps-and-Priority-Queues Min/Max Heaps, Heapify, extraction. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 06-Hashing-and-Tries Hash Maps, Hash Sets, Prefix Trie search. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 07-Graphs-and-Disjoint-Set Adjacency lists/matrices, BFS, DFS, Disjoint Set (DSU). 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 08-Sorting-and-Searching Binary search, Merge Sort, Quick Sort, Bubble/Selection. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 09-Greedy-Algorithms Fractional Knapsack, Activity Selection. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 10-Dynamic-Programming Overlapping subproblems, Memoization, Tabulation, LCS. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 11-Backtracking-and-Bit-Manipulation N-Queens, subsets generation, bitwise tricks. 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS 12-Advanced-Data-Structures Segment Trees, Fenwick Trees (BIT). 🐍 Python, 🟦 C++, ☕ Java, 🟨 JS

docs.title: 📁 Directory Structure Model
docs.text:
Each module folder is structured cleanly as follows: 

📂 <module-name>/
├── 📝 README.md               # Visual concept guide, cheat sheets & complexity tables
├── 📂 python/                 # Python implementations (.py)
├── 📂 cpp/                    # C++ source files (.cpp)
├── 📂 java/                   # Java class source files (.java)
└── 📂 js/                     # JavaScript files runnable via Node.js (.js)

docs.title: 🚀 Execution Quickstart Guide
docs.text: All implementations include self-contained test cases. To run any implementation, follow these steps:

docs.title: 🐍 Python 3
docs.text: python3 python/solution.py

docs.title: 🟦 C++ (GCC Compiler)
docs.text:
Compile and execute using any standard C++ compiler: 

g++ -std=c++17 cpp/solution.cpp -o solution
./solution

docs.title: ☕ Java
docs.text:
Compile and run the Java source file: 

javac java/Solution.java
java Solution

docs.title: 🟨 JavaScript (Node.js)
docs.text:
Execute the script using Node.js: 

node js/solution.js

docs.title: ⚡ Big-O Complexity Summary Reference
docs.text:
Here is a quick cheat sheet for data structure operations:

Data Structure Access Search Insertion Deletion Space Array \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) Stack \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) Queue \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) Singly Linked List \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) Doubly Linked List \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) Binary Search Tree (BST) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(N)\) Min/Max Heap - \(O(N)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(N)\) Hash Table - \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\)

docs.title: Module 00: Foundations and Complexity Analysis
docs.text: Welcome to the Foundations and Complexity Analysis module. This section covers basic language constructs (patterns, loops, condition handling) and focuses on the theoretical groundwork of Big-O complexity analysis.

docs.title: Time Complexity
docs.text: Refers to the computation time required by an algorithm as a function of input size (\(N\)). * Worst-Case (\(O\)): Maximum time taken (upper bound). * Best-Case (\(\Omega\)): Minimum time taken (lower bound). * Average-Case (\(\Theta\)): Expected average execution time.

docs.title: Space Complexity
docs.text: Memory required by an algorithm to execute, including input space and auxiliary space (extra space utilized during execution, such as recursion stack frames).

docs.title: Complexity Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Time Complexity Name Example Algorithm \(O(1)\) Constant Array indexing, basic arithmetic \(O(\log N)\) Logarithmic Binary Search, Heap operations \(O(N)\) Linear Linear Search, Array traversal \(O(N \log N)\) Linearithmic Merge Sort, Quick Sort (avg) \(O(N^2)\) Quadratic Bubble Sort, Selection Sort \(O(2^N)\) Exponential Recursive Fibonacci, Subsets generation \(O(N!)\) Factorial N-Queens backtracking, permutations

docs.title: Module 01: Arrays and Strings
docs.text: This module covers 1D and 2D arrays, matrix operations, two-pointers, sliding window patterns, and string parsing.

docs.title: 1D and 2D Arrays
docs.text: An array is a collection of elements identified by index or key. In memory, arrays are stored in contiguous blocks, which allows \(O(1)\) lookup but makes insertion/deletion \(O(N)\). * 1D Arrays: Standard flat sequences of values. * 2D Arrays (Matrices): Grid structures stored in row-major or column-major form.

docs.title: Algorithmic Patterns
docs.text:
• Two Pointers: Using two variables pointing to different array indices to optimize nested loops. (e.g., palindrome validation, subset finding).
  • Sliding Window: Maintaining a subsegment (window) that expands or shrinks to find subarrays matching criteria (e.g., maximum sum subarray of size K).

docs.title: Operations Complexity
docs.text: Operation Time Complexity (Array) Time Complexity (String) Access \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) Search \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) Insertion \(O(N)\) (requires shifting) \(O(N)\) Deletion \(O(N)\) (requires shifting) \(O(N)\)

docs.title: Module 02: Linked Lists
docs.text: A Linked List is a linear data structure where elements are stored in nodes. Unlike arrays, nodes are not stored in contiguous memory but are chained via pointer links.

docs.title: Singly Linked List
docs.text:
Each node contains a data payload and a single pointer (next) to the succeeding node. 

[ Head: data | next ] ---> [ data | next ] ---> [ data | null ]

docs.title: Doubly Linked List
docs.text:
Each node contains data, next, and a prev pointer referencing the previous node. 

[ null ] <--- [ prev | data | next ] <=> [ prev | data | next ] ---> [ null ]

docs.title: Circular Linked List
docs.text: The tail node's next pointer links back to the head node.

docs.title: Operations Complexity
docs.text: Operation Worst-Case Best-Case Access / Search \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\) Insert at Head \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) Insert at Tail \(O(N)\) (or \(O(1)\) with tail pointer) \(O(1)\) Delete by Value \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\)

docs.title: Module 03: Stacks and Queues
docs.text: This module explores linear data structures utilizing restricted access rules.

docs.title: Stack (LIFO - Last In, First Out)
docs.text: Elements are inserted and removed from the same end, called the "top". * Push: Inserts an element on top. * Pop: Removes the top element. * Peek: Views the top element without removing it.

docs.title: Queue (FIFO - First In, First Out)
docs.text: Elements are inserted at the back ("rear") and removed from the front ("front"). * Enqueue: Inserts an element at the rear. * Dequeue: Removes the front element.

docs.title: Deque (Double-Ended Queue)
docs.text: Supports insertions and deletions from both front and rear.

docs.title: Complexity Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Operation Stack Queue Deque Push/Enqueue \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) Pop/Dequeue \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) Peek \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\) \(O(1)\)

docs.title: Module 04: Trees and Binary Search Trees (BST)
docs.text: Trees are hierarchical structures containing nodes connected by edges, starting from a single "root" node.

docs.title: Binary Tree
docs.text: Each node has at most two children (left and right). * Traversals: * Pre-order (DFS): Root -> Left -> Right * In-order (DFS): Left -> Root -> Right (Produces sorted order in BST) * Post-order (DFS): Left -> Right -> Root * Level-order (BFS): Layer by layer from top to bottom

docs.title: Binary Search Tree (BST)
docs.text: A binary tree enforcing: $\(\text{Left Child} < \text{Parent} < \text{Right Child}\)$

docs.title: Complexity Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Operation Average Case (BST) Worst Case (Skewed BST) Search \(O(\log N)\) \(O(N)\) Insertion \(O(\log N)\) \(O(N)\) Deletion \(O(\log N)\) \(O(N)\)

docs.title: Module 05: Heaps and Priority Queues
docs.text: A Heap is a complete binary tree structure used for fast minimum/maximum retrieval.

docs.title: Heap Properties
docs.text:
• Min Heap: The key at the root must be the minimum among all keys present in the Binary Heap. This property holds recursively for all subtrees.
  • Max Heap: The key at the root must be the maximum among all keys.

docs.title: Complexity Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Operation Time Complexity Details Peek Min/Max \(O(1)\) Direct access to root Insert \(O(\log N)\) Adds to end, then heapifies up Extract Min/Max \(O(\log N)\) Replaces root with last element, then heapifies down Heapify (Build) \(O(N)\) Bottom-up heap construction

docs.title: Module 06: Hashing and Tries
docs.text: This module focuses on key-value lookups using Hash Maps, Sets, and prefix matching using Tries.

docs.title: Hashing
docs.text: Converts arbitrary keys into indices of a fixed-size table via a Hash Function. * Collision Resolution: Chaining (linked list buckets) and Open Addressing (linear/quadratic probing, double hashing).

docs.title: Trie (Prefix Tree)
docs.text: A specialized tree structure used to store strings. Each node represents a character, allowing fast prefix-based lookups.

docs.title: Complexity Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Operation Hash Map (Average) Hash Map (Worst) Trie (Word length \(L\)) Insertion \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(L)\) Search \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(L)\) Deletion \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(L)\)

docs.title: Module 07: Graphs and Disjoint Set
docs.text: Graphs consist of a finite set of vertices (nodes) and edges (connections).

docs.title: Representation
docs.text:
• Adjacency Matrix: 2D array indicating edges (\(O(1)\) lookup, \(O(V^2)\) space).
  • Adjacency List: Array of lists mapping neighbors (\(O(V+E)\) space).

docs.title: Traversal
docs.text:
• BFS (Breadth-First Search): Explores neighbors level-by-level using a Queue.
  • DFS (Depth-First Search): Explores paths deeply before backtracking using Recursion/Stack.

docs.title: Disjoint Set Union (DSU)
docs.text: A data structure tracking partition groupings, optimized with Path Compression and Union by Rank.

docs.title: Traversals Complexity
docs.text: Algorithm Time Complexity Space Complexity BFS \(O(V + E)\) \(O(V)\) DFS \(O(V + E)\) \(O(V)\)

docs.title: Module 08: Sorting and Searching
docs.text: This module covers foundational search algorithms and sorting techniques.

docs.title: Algorithms Complexity
docs.text: Algorithm Best Case Average Case Worst Case Space Complexity Stable Linear Search \(O(1)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(N)\) \(O(1)\) Yes Binary Search \(O(1)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(\log N)\) \(O(1)\) N/A Bubble Sort \(O(N)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(1)\) Yes Selection Sort \(O(N^2)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(1)\) No Insertion Sort \(O(N)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(1)\) Yes Merge Sort \(O(N \log N)\) \(O(N \log N)\) \(O(N \log N)\) \(O(N)\) Yes Quick Sort \(O(N \log N)\) \(O(N \log N)\) \(O(N^2)\) \(O(\log N)\) No

docs.title: Module 09: Greedy Algorithms
docs.text: Greedy algorithms build up a solution piece by piece, always choosing the next piece that offers the most immediate benefit.

docs.title: Key Properties
docs.text:
1. Greedy Choice Property: A global optimal solution can be arrived at by making locally optimal (greedy) choices.
  2. Optimal Substructure: An optimal solution to the problem contains optimal solutions to its subproblems.

docs.title: Classic Problems
docs.text:
• Activity Selection: Maximize non-overlapping intervals (Sorted by end time, \(O(N \log N)\)).
  • Fractional Knapsack: Maximize knapsack value by sorting items by value-to-weight ratio and picking fractions.

docs.title: Module 10: Dynamic Programming (DP)
docs.text: Dynamic Programming is an algorithmic technique for solving optimization problems by breaking them down into simpler sub-problems and utilizing overlapping subsolutions.

docs.title: Key Approaches
docs.text:
• Top-Down (Memoization): Solves recursively and stores computed solutions in a cache.
  • Bottom-Up (Tabulation): Builds a table iteratively starting from base cases.

docs.title: Classic Patterns
docs.text:
• Fibonacci Sequence
  • Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
  • 0/1 Knapsack

docs.title: Module 11: Backtracking and Bit Manipulation
docs.text: This module combines exhaustive state search patterns and bitwise algorithmic tricks.

docs.title: Backtracking
docs.text: Systematically searches all configurations of a state space. It abandons a candidate path ("backtracks") as soon as it determines the candidate cannot lead to a valid solution (e.g. N-Queens, Subsets, Permutations).

docs.title: Bit Manipulation
docs.text: Performs operations directly on binary bits (\(O(1)\) time complexity). * Check Power of Two: n & (n - 1) == 0 * Toggle Bit: n ^ (1 << i) * Single Number Detection: XOR accumulator properties (x ^ x = 0).

docs.title: Module 12: Advanced Data Structures
docs.text: Welcome to Advanced Data Structures, which covers query optimization on intervals.

docs.title: Segment Tree
docs.text:
A binary tree used for storing intervals or segments. It allows querying a range and updating a point in \(O(\log N)\) time. 

            [0-5] (Sum=36)
           /              \
     [0-2] (16)         [3-5] (20)
     /        \        /        \
  [0-1] (9)  [2] (7) [3-4] (14) [5] (6)

docs.title: Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree - BIT)
docs.text: A compact data structure representing prefix sum frequencies in \(O(\log N)\) time with minimal memory overhead (\(O(N)\) space).
